definitions: A complication of diabetes that affects the eyes, caused by damage to the blood vessels of the light-sensitive tissue at the back of the eye (retina).
A leading cause of blindness in adults, characterized by the leakage of fluid or blood from retinal blood vessels, or the growth of new, abnormal blood vessels on the retina.
examples: Early detection of diabetic retinopathy is crucial.
Laser treatment can help manage diabetic retinopathy.
Regular eye exams are important for preventing diabetic retinopathy.
